channel.title: Snorly Blog
channel.description: Plain answers about snoring: how to know if you snore, what it sounds like, what makes it worse and how to check whether a fix worked. By the makers of Snorly.

item.title: Do anti-snoring pillows work? Tested by recording
item.description: Memory foam cut snoring events 47% in a sleep-lab trial; an inclined pillow cut breathing events from 17 to 5 an hour. Which pillows have data, how to test yours.

item.title: Does mouth tape stop snoring? How to test it safely
item.description: Mouth tape cut snoring by about half in small studies of mouth breathers with mild apnea. Here is who should skip it, and a 7-night way to test it on yourself.

item.title: Do nasal strips work for snoring? What recordings show
item.description: Nasal strips cut snores per hour from 258 to 173 in the one placebo-controlled trial, but only with a blocked nose. How to test a strip on yourself in 7 nights.

item.title: Best Snoring Apps for iPhone: 6 Compared, Free Tiers
item.description: Six snoring apps compared on what they record, whether you can play clips back for free, privacy and price model. We make Snorly, so the bias is disclosed.

item.title: How to tell if you snore when you sleep alone
item.description: Record three nights with your phone on the nightstand and listen to the clips in the morning. A dry mouth is a hint; the recording is the answer.

item.title: How to Record Yourself Snoring on iPhone: Memos vs App
item.description: Put the iPhone on the nightstand 0.5 to 1 m away, plugged in, on Do Not Disturb. Voice Memos gives one 8-hour file to scrub; a snore app keeps only the clips.

item.title: How to Sleep When Your Partner Snores (Without a Fight)
item.description: Record one night and play the clip back calmly, then check for gasps. Then foam earplugs (about 13 dB in practice), white noise, side sleeping, or a spare room.

item.title: How to stop snoring: 9 fixes ranked by evidence
item.description: Sleep on your side, stop alcohol 2 to 3 hours before bed, clear your nose and manage weight; a mouthpiece or CPAP for the rest. How to test each in 3 nights.

item.title: Sleep Talking App: Record What You Say in Your Sleep
item.description: Put your iPhone on the nightstand with a sound-triggered recorder and you get time-stamped clips of talking instead of an 8-hour file. What the clips mean.

item.title: What causes snoring in women, and what changes it
item.description: Snoring in women rises with menopause, pregnancy (about 1 in 4 by the last weeks), nasal congestion, weight and alcohol. What to check and how to measure a fix.

item.title: Snoring vs Sleep Apnea: The Difference on a Recording
item.description: Plain snoring is a steady sound. Sleep apnea sounds like a snore, 10 seconds of silence, then a gasp. How to spot the pattern, score STOP-BANG and get tested.

item.title: What does snoring sound like? Decibels and types
item.description: Hear real recordings of light, moderate and severe snoring and of a 32-second breathing pause. Loud snoring runs 50 to 90 dB; the record is 111.6 dB.

item.title: Why do I snore? Find your cause in 5 nights
item.description: You snore because relaxed throat tissue vibrates in a narrowed airway. Seven causes narrow it; five tagged, recorded nights show which one is yours.
